newsitem.title: SYRIA: EU proposes new formula to revive Syria talks.
newsitem.headline: EU proposes new formula to revive Syria talks.

text.p: The European Union's Middle East envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos has presented Syria with a formula to revive Damascus's peace talks with Israel which broke off a year ago, officials said on Monday.
They said the EU's proposal, based on full withdrawal for full security, was presented by Moratinos during talks in Damascus on Sunday night with Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara.
"The formula calls for total withdrawal from the occupied Arab lands in return for total, equal and mutual security for both parties," a Syrian official said.
An official accompanying Moratinos told Reuters before the EU envoy headed to Beirut for similar talks with Lebanese leaders that the talks were "very positive".
"Things are a bit sensitive at this stage and we hope to have more to say at a later stage," the official said.
Moratinos said he was too busy to talk to the press.

Western diplomats said the EU formula would be favourable for Syria which is mainly interested in Israel's full withdrawal from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967. Syria also believes that peace would ensure security for all.

"Syria wants full withdrawal from its occupied lands. The current Israeli goverment of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is most concerned about security. Syria does not object to this because it wants total security for all parties," one diplomat said.
The United States is the main sponsor of the Arab-Israeli peace talks but Syria and other Arab states support a greator European role in the negotiations.
Moratinos said earlier that he was in full coordination with the U.S. over his mission in the region briefing Washington on the outcome of his talks.
Syria has strongly condemned netanyahu for refusing to swap occupied Arab lands for peace, a formula on which the Arab-Israeli peace negotiations were based when the talks opened in Madrid in 1991.
